summary: Kalyan Kumar Sarkar is a scholar of Indology, archaeology, history, and linguistics who studied under Prabodh Chandra Bagchi. He served as a professor at the University of Windsor (attested 2002).

Kamala Tiyavanich is a historian and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Cornell University under David K. Wyatt, A. Thomas Kirsch, and Richard Polenberg. She held a Mellon Postdoctoral Fellowship at Cornell University from 1993 to 1994.
Kamaleswar Bhattacharya (1928–2014) was an Indologist and philosopher. He held academic posts at Brown University, the University of Toronto, and the University of Bonn.

Kamil Zvelebil (1927–2009) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Charles University (~1946–1952). He worked at the Oriental Institute of the ASCR (~1952–1968) and Utrecht University (1980–1990).

Kamlesh Dutt Tripathi is an Indologist and religious studies scholar who held posts at Banaras Hindu University and served as an advisor at the Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts (attested 2009).

Kammie Takahashi is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at Mount Holyoke College and the University of Virginia under David Germano and Paul Groner, later holding a post at Muhlenberg College in 2011.

Kanai Lal Hazra (born 1932) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. He studied under Sukumar Sengupta and completed his PhD at the University of Ceylon under Sirima Kiribamune, later serving as Lecturer in Pali at the University of Calcutta.
Kanchu Onoue is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a teacher at Hikone Higashi High School (attested 1963) and as a professor at Eizan Gakuin (attested 1976).

Kang-nam Oh is a religious studies and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at the University of Tokyo (1973–1974) and under doctoral supervisor Yun-hua Jan, later holding a post at the University of Regina (attested 1990–1998).
Kang-yuan Sung is a religious studies and Buddhist studies scholar. He completed an MA at the University of Calgary under supervisor A. W. Barber and also studied under Leslie S. Kawamura.
Kangei Okamoto (1899–1948) was a Buddhist studies and history/archaeology scholar. He studied under Takamatsu Yoshie and at the University of Paris, and later worked at the Tokyo National Museum.
Kanoko Tanaka is an Indologist and religious studies scholar who studied under Muni Tulsi. She served as a part-time lecturer in religious studies at Komazawa University (attested 2001).
Kansei Tamura (1928–2018) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo and served as a lecturer at Rissho University (attested 1962).

Kapila Vatsyayan (1928–2020) was an Indologist and historian. She studied at the University of Delhi, University of Michigan, and Banaras Hindu University, and served as Academic Director of the Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts (~1987–2000).

Karel Werner (1925–2019) was an Indologist and philosopher. In 1968, he taught Sanskrit and Indian Philosophy and Religion at Durham University and Cambridge University, later serving as an Honorary Professorial Research Associate at SOAS (~1993–2019).

Karen C. Lang is an Indologist, Tibetologist, and Buddhist studies scholar. She studied at Banaras Hindu University, the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives, and the University of Washington, and served as a professor at the University of Virginia.
Karen McCarthy Brown (1942–2015) was a religious studies scholar who studied at Smith College (~1960–1964), Union Theological Seminary (~1964–1966), and Temple University (~1971–1976).

Karen Nelson Villanueva is a scholar of philosophy and religious studies. She earned her PhD at the California Institute of Integral Studies (attested 2013) and studied under Geshe Ngawang Dakpa and Lobsang Chökyi.
Karen Nero is a scholar who has held academic posts at the University of Canterbury and the University of Otago.

Karen O'Brien-Kop works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She earned her PhD at SOAS University of London, where she worked as a senior teaching fellow, and lectured at the University of Roehampton (attested 2020).
